stem_book: Passage Q.(i) to (iii). Enthalpy alone or entropy alone is not enough to decide spontaneity; Gibbs energy, ΔG = ΔH − TΔS, combines both with temperature. A decrease in Gibbs energy is a measure of the useful work a system can do and of spontaneity; ΔG is zero for a system at equilibrium. (i) The lattice energy of a salt AB is 764 kJ and its hydration energy is 755 kJ. If the entropy of dissolution of AB in water is 40 J/K/mol at 298 K, the Gibbs energy change of dissolution is (a) 9.0 kJ (b) −2.92 kJ (c) −11.2 kJ (d) −9.0 kJ. (ii) If 20 g argon is compressed from 10 L to 5 L under reversible isothermal conditions at 300 K, the Gibbs energy change would be [R = 8.3 J; at. mass Ar = 40; ideal behaviour] (a) −2.59 kJ (b) 0.863 kJ (c) −0.863 kJ (d) 1.98 kJ. (iii) If the standard Gibbs energy change of a system is zero, the equilibrium constant would be (a) 100 (b) Zero (c) 10.0 (d) 1.0
